tool: optimization_una_cpu/tools/probe_laptop.py plus direct system probes (sysctl, vm_stat, df, uptime)

platform.isa: arm64 (Apple silicon, no x86 emulation observed)

cpu.cpu_quota: none observable (macOS has no cgroup cpu.max; taskpolicy not applied)
cpu.notes: Two of the ten logical cores are efficiency cores; sustained-throughput budget therefore conservatively admitted as C=8.

memory.notes: Machine shared with unrelated user work; load average 7.23/5.36/4.47 at inventory (15-day uptime, 21 terminal users). Memory pressure non-trivial: swap 3.4 GiB of 4 GiB used.

disk.data_volume_free_bytes: 142 GiB reported by df -h /Users (Data volume, 68% capacity)

admitted_resource_budget.cpu_budget_basis: sum(workers_i * effective_threads_i) <= 8 for all benchmark arms; efficiency cores excluded from sustained budget conservatively; no hard quota exists on macOS so this is a self-imposed policy recorded in advance
admitted_resource_budget.ram_policy: single-job process-tree peak measured before any W>1; safety margin maintained against 16 GiB total with concurrent user load; queue depth bounded; one process owns one output directory
admitted_resource_budget.benchmark_exclusivity: no other campaign build/test/profile runs while the benchmark owner executes; unrelated user processes outside campaign control are recorded via load-average samples, not evicted

python.system_python: 3.14.7 (homebrew) - no scientific deps installed, unusable for campaign
python.numba_threading_layer: to be recorded after first import in dependency record (NUMA/threading layer probed at runtime)
